label: Software engineering
sub: Built for a full-time search: mornings on data structures and algorithms, afternoons on applications, system design, and behavioral practice.
weighting: This track covers the three rounds most software engineering loops use, at any level: system design starts in week 2 on home turf and runs two cases a week from week 3; behavioral prep centers on ownership, collaboration, and measurable results; algorithms stay daily because most loops still open with a coding screen. Shift the mix toward your target role — more design for infrastructure and backend, more front-end fundamentals for UI roles, fewer design cases for early-career loops.
rules: Set a 30-minute timer per problem. If you're stuck at 20 minutes, read the approach (not the code), then write it yourself. Log every problem's pattern in a notebook — the pattern is what transfers, not the problem.

resources.d: Patterns in order; the 150 list is the study spine
Timed practice; use company tags once interviews are scheduled
Free and end to end: resume, algorithm cheat sheets, behavioral
The free reference for design fundamentals and case studies
System design walkthroughs at the level interviewers grade against
Anonymous mocks with working engineers; closest thing to the real loop
Comp by company and level, for targeting and negotiating
Kleppmann. Chapters 5–6 (replication, partitioning) are the high-yield ones

schedule.h: Open this page. Clear the follow-ups due, pick today's three target roles, choose the problem set.
Three problems, 30 minutes each on a timer, then 15 minutes reviewing the optimal solution and logging the pattern.
Three to five applications, each tailored: swap 2–3 resume bullets to match the posting. Log every one here before moving on.
Five messages: referrals, recruiters, alumni. Send every follow-up that is due today.
Pattern flashcards, note what was hard, write tomorrow's three targets. Then stop — rest is part of the plan.

1.h: One case out loud, 40 minutes, then 30 minutes reading what you missed. Draw it — boxes, arrows, numbers.

2.h: STAR stories on a timer, recorded. Listen back for rambling and missing results. Then rehearse the project deep-dive.

3.h: One case out loud, 40 minutes, then 30 minutes reading what you missed. Draw it — boxes, arrows, numbers.

4.h: STAR stories on a timer, recorded. Listen back for rambling and missing results. Then rehearse the project deep-dive.

5.h: Book a mock (coding and design on alternate weeks). At 4:00, retro: applications sent, response rate by source, what changes next week.

0.h: Set up Monday before bed: the week's target companies and problem list. Nothing else.

6.h: One problem, one mock if it's scheduled, then rest.
